scientific_summary: For independent heterogeneous proportional-hazards components with an unknown common baseline, the two marginal laws of the first and second failure times identify the unknown component count, all normalized hazard multipliers up to permutation, and the aggregate baseline. Either marginal alone identifies none of the relative hazard information. The identification reduces exactly to uniqueness of a finite signed exponential sum.
limitations: Population-level semiparametric identification only. Independence, a common continuous PHR baseline, and strictly positive multipliers are required. Numerical inversion can be ill-conditioned for nearly equal hazards. The complete Pledger--Proschan (1971) chapter was not inspected theorem by theorem, leaving residual originality risk from older reliability literature.
